title: Polyglot toolcall gateway: name resolution, streaming boundaries, and structured-output harmonization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers use a mix of OpenAI-style 'tool' contracts and legacy 'functions' surface shapes. Differences include naming conventions (snake_case vs camelCase), parameter ordering, optional/required flags, streaming semantics (interleaved chunk vs final call metadata), and structured-output expectations. We need a runtime gateway layer that can accept incoming invocation requests targeted at Redwood API and reliably interoperate with downstream runtime handlers and external tool integration endpoints without requiring callers to rewrite prompts or tool definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts both OpenAI-style tool descriptors and legacy function descriptors and returns successful invocations for >=95% of synthetic mapping cases in test harness
Name mismatch resolution implemented using alias table + fuzzy heuristics with opt-out header; latency added by gateway <3ms p50
Streaming behavior preserved: gateway can translate between chunked tool-call streaming (OpenAI) and legacy per-message function invocation with correct end-of-stream markers
Structured output mapping supports field remapping rules and validation against expected JSON schema; failures surfaced with clear error codes and guidance
Canary rollout completed to 5% of internal traffic, no regressions in existing customers' integration tests and telemetry shows <0.1% invoke-errors attributable to gateway
tasks: Design alias table format and storage (Redis vs Postgres schema) and TTL/metrics for automatic alias promotion
Prototype fuzzy name resolution module (Levenshtein + tokenizer heuristics + telemetry-weighted aliases)
Implement streaming translator: map OpenAI chunk stream frames to internal event stream and ensure chunk ordering + EOS handling
Implement structured-output mapper with declarative remapping rules and JSONSchema-backed validation
Add per-route compatibility flags (header/route config) and opt-out mechanism for strict mode
End-to-end tests covering name collisions, intentionally ambiguous tool names, and cross-protocol fallbacks
Instrument telemetry: resolution path chosen, latency, number of remapped fields, errors and auto-accept promotions
Create migration/runbook for customer-facing changes and a canary/rollout plan
decisions: Will implement alias store in Postgres with a fast hot cache in Redis to allow human-driven overrides and telemetry backfill
Fuzzy match algorithm: primary key is exact -> normalized (strip punctuation, lower) -> longest common subsequence -> Levenshtein as tie-breaker
Streaming translate will punctuate internal stream with canonical 'invocation_eos' event for downstreams that expect final metadata
Structured output mapping uses declarative rules (source_field -> target_field) and will support type coercions for common scalar conversions
Compatibility mode default is permissive; strict mode must be opt-in via route config or header to avoid breaking existing integrations

notes_for_release_engineering: Add feature flag 'polyglot-tool-gateway' default on for internal tenants; expose opt-out header X-Redwood-Tool-Gateway: off for external customers during early rollout. Ensure Redis cluster capacity increased before canary.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal-only traffic (dev + staging) for 3 days with synthetic traffic harness
Stage 2: Canary 5% of production, monitoring for errors and latency for 48h
Stage 3: 25% if stable, run compatibility test suite against top 50 customers' manifests
Stage 4: Gradual 100% over 1 week with rollback plan and customer communication template ready
